question: Should OpenClaw adopt a core path-scoped filesystem policy now, and must its first supported contract cover shell-mediated filesystem access or explicitly remain file-tool-only?
rationale: Current main has only a workspace boolean, while the two active implementation candidates propose incompatible contracts and intentionally leave arbitrary exec unchanged; only maintainers can define the product promise and security boundary.

options.title: Design one unified core policy
options.body: Specify a canonical `tools.fs` contract and require complete, honest semantics for file tools, media, subagents, sandboxing, and exec limitations before landing an implementation.

options.title: Land a file-tool-only policy
options.body: Choose one candidate contract for file and media tools while prominently documenting that arbitrary exec remains outside the filesystem boundary.

options.title: Keep enforcement at the OS boundary
options.body: Decline granular core path policy and continue requiring containers, VMs, separate users, or another sandbox backend for filesystem isolation.

recommendation.title: Design one unified core policy
recommendation.body: Specify a canonical `tools.fs` contract and require complete, honest semantics for file tools, media, subagents, sandboxing, and exec limitations before landing an implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The current filesystem policy and its central refactors trace directly to his commits, making him the strongest available owner for the permanent boundary decision.
